title: IAM schema migrations at service boot
name: Identity schema migrator

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code applies and records IAM schema migrations? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: The version row is inserted before BEGIN, so it autocommits on its own. If up() then fails, the ROLLBACK undoes the schema change but not the version record. On the next boot max(version) already includes the failed migration, so it is skipped forever and the schema silently lacks it (for example, the unique constraint in 42 would never be created). The INSERT belongs inside the transaction, after up() succeeds.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Migration 42 runs against a table that has two bindings with the same principal, role and scope, ids 10 and 17. What happens?
choices: The constraint creation fails because of the duplicate
Both rows are deleted, then the constraint is added
Row 17 is deleted, row 10 is kept, and the constraint is added
Row 10 is deleted, row 17 is kept, and the constraint is added
choiceQuestions.explanation: The DELETE ... USING removes `a` where a.id > b.id among matching rows, so the higher id (17) goes and 10 stays, after which the unique constraint can be created. It does not fail, does not delete both, and keeps the lower id rather than the higher.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Three replicas of the identity service boot at once with migrations 41-43 pending. How do they interact?
choices: All three run 41 at once and two fail on ALTER TABLE
One acquires the advisory lock and applies them; the others wait, then see max(version)=43 and apply nothing
The first to boot applies them; the others exit because the lock is held
choiceQuestions.explanation: pg_advisory_lock blocks until released. The waiting replicas then re-read max(version), which is 43, so pending is empty. They do not run concurrently, they do not exit on contention (that would need pg_try_advisory_lock), and work is not split.

choiceQuestions.prompt: While migration 41 runs on a large role_bindings table, what does it mean for authorization checks reading that table?
choices: They are unaffected because ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN takes no lock
They block until the migration's transaction commits, because ALTER TABLE holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the whole transaction including the full-table UPDATE
They see scope = NULL for some rows until the transaction commits
They fail immediately with a lock timeout
choiceQuestions.explanation: ALTER TABLE takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock held until COMMIT, and 41 runs the full-table UPDATE and further ALTERs in the same transaction, so readers block for the entire duration. They are not unaffected, they cannot see uncommitted NULLs, and there is no lock_timeout configured for them to fail fast.
